mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which boosts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with wage pressures, which can lead to inflation and monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a month, it signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative for 2 quarters and HOUST declines > 10% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% over three months signals inflationary pressures, which can lead to monetary tightening and reduced corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 5% in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5%, it signals a weakening consumer demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines > 5% in 1 month and UNRATE rises > 0.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.
